spark.byteSummary:
Learn how Kubernetes reconciles desired state through etcd, the API server, scheduler, kubelet, Services, and readiness probes.

Every component watches the API Server (backed by Raft-based etcd) and executes level-triggered reconciliation loops.

Strong Kubernetes engineering focuses on control-plane mechanics, zero-downtime rollouts with PodDisruptionBudgets, and resource-aware scheduling.

qaDetails.summary: Why do clients briefly see 502s during a rolling deploy even with graceful SIGTERM handling?
qaDetails.body: Endpoint removal from kube-proxy/Ingress happens asynchronously in parallel with SIGTERM. Adding a `preStop: sleep 5` hook gives load balancers time to drain before the app stops listening.

qaDetails.summary: Why should Liveness probes never check external dependencies like Postgres or Redis?
qaDetails.body: If Postgres blips for 10 seconds, Liveness kills and restarts every healthy app pod simultaneously, turning a minor DB hiccup into a full outage.

knowledgeCheck.question: What happens when a container exceeds its Kubernetes memory limit vs. its CPU limit?

options.text: A. Both result in immediate OOMKill
options.feedback: CPU is compressible and is throttled rather than killed.

options.text: B. Memory excess triggers OOMKill (exit 137); CPU excess triggers CFS throttling
options.feedback: Correct! Memory is incompressible (OOMKill), while CPU is throttled by the kernel CFS quota.
Memory cannot be throttled safely and triggers the Linux OOM killer.

tipsAndTricks: Never include downstream DB/cache checks in a Liveness probe—only in Readiness.
Add a short `preStop` sleep (e.g., 5s) before handling SIGTERM so Ingress/kube-proxy stops routing new connections first.
Set `TopologySpreadConstraints` and `PodDisruptionBudget` on production deployments so a single AZ or node drain doesn't drop capacity.
finalSummaryEyebrow: The idea to keep with you
finalSummaryTitle: Set realistic requests/limits, isolate readiness from liveness, and design pods to terminate gracefully.
finalSummary: Strong Kubernetes engineering focuses on control-plane mechanics, zero-downtime rollouts with PodDisruptionBudgets, and resource-aware scheduling.
